item.title: 44 Years Later, Steven Spielberg's Scariest Movie of All Time Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.description: Poltergeist , which became available to stream for free on Pluto TV on Nov. 1 , follows an ordinary suburban family that begins to experience strange things in their home. Furniture and toys move on their own, a glass of milk shatters out of nowhere, and the youngest child in the family, 5-year-old Carol Anne (Heather O'Rourke), begins to communicate with beings through the television. At first, these events are dismissed, but during a thunderstorm one night, a tree outside the windows of the kids’ room crashes in and snatches the boy. Then, a portal opens in their closet, sucking Carol Anne into another dimension. With help from some paranormal investigators, the family tries everything to bring her back.

item.title: Texans’ C.J. Stroud draws intriguing Joe Burrow comparison
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Texans’ C.J. Stroud draws intriguing Joe Burrow comparison appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans are now 4-6 on the season after stomping the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on “Thursday Night Football” in Week 11 thanks to another solid outing from quarterback C.J. Stroud. While the 25-year-old signal-caller has yet to sign a contract extension with the club, he is at least doing his part to keep the team competitive. After another good game, Colin Cowherd couldn’t help but compare Stroud to Joe Burrow . Cowherd’s comparison had more to do with the contract situation for Burrow right before he signed his five-year, $275 million extension. The popular sports analyst claims that the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t do enough to build around Burrow before giving him his extension, and feels Stroud is in a similar situation with the Texans. “C.J. Stroud has had a great season, and now the Texans are trapped,” Cowherd said… “I feel like he’s going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn’t get it done enough before he signed the big deal.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "C.J. Stroud has had a great season and now the Texans are trapped… I feel like he's going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn't get it done enough before he signed the big deal." @colincowherd on C.J. Stroud & the Texans pic.twitter.com/Of7YQ5dM0Y — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) November 20, 2026 The Texans initially went into the 2026-27 campaign believed to have the best defense in football, while questions surrounded Stroud about whether or not he is a franchise quarterback. Fast forward to Week 11, and the storyline is seemingly the opposite. Even though Houston has struggled throughout the campaign, the four-year veteran is putting up solid numbers, throwing for 2,656 yards, 22 touchdowns, and four interceptions with a 64.0% completion percentage through 10 games. Stroud is well on pace to throw for the most touchdowns in a single season in his career, as he’s just one shy of tying his career record of 23 set in his rookie year. If the defense can somehow get to the level of play it was last season, then the Texans could be a huge problem in the back end of the 2026-27 campaign. C.J. Stroud and his teammates will enjoy a mini-bye after playing on TNF. Houston will next play in Week 12 at home against the Baltimore Ravens. item.title: Knicks superfan Ben Stiller recalls losing his mind over Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. Pistons in 2025 playoffs
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images. Knicks superfan Ben Stiller recalls losing his mind over Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. Pistons in 2025 playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of the most memorable moments of New York Knicks superfan Ben Stiller was Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. the Detroit Pistons during the 2025 playoffs. A fan responded to a post asking what the “greatest” non- OG Anunoby tip-in play in Knicks history was. One fan responded with a clip of Brunson’s game-winner in Game 6 of the Knicks-Pistons series last year, saying, “This s**t literally made Me lose my mind,” to which Stiller replied, “Me too.” Me too. https://t.co/NiNxCoU521 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Ben Stiller (@BenStiller) November 20, 2026 The play was huge. The game was tied at 113 before Brunson hit his three-pointer with about four seconds left in the game. Detroit was unable to score on their next possession. Brunson ended the game with 40 points. He also had four rebounds and seven assists. He was the Knicks’ leading scorer that night. This won the series for the Knicks, who advance to the Eastern Conference Semifinals. They made it all the way to the Eastern Conference Finals that year before losing to the Indiana Pacers. The following year, the Knicks made it to the NBA Finals. They beat the San Antonio Spurs in five games to win their first championship in 53 years. Stiller is one of the most famous celebrity fans of the Knicks. He has been filming footage for an upcoming documentary about the team dating back to their playoff run earlier in 2026. The Knicks have gotten back on track after a disastrous 0-3 start. They have won three games in a row, including two straight against the Toronto Raptors, and just beat the Minnesota Timberwolves. They survived a four-game road trip and will play their next five games at home, including a Black Friday matchup with the Miami Heat. The Knicks will also play the Portland Trail Blazers, the Pacers, the Cleveland Cavaliers, and the Atlanta Hawks in this home stretch. item.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
item.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

item.title: Naomi Osaka issues statement as her 2026 season ends after ‘extreme eye-opener’ this year
item.description: Naomi Osaka’s 2026 season came to an end last month in front of a home crowd in Tokyo. The Japanese star played just 13 tournaments this year, including all four Grand Slams and six WTA 1000 events. But following the resurgent second half of her 2025 season, during which she made the semifinals of the US Open and the final of the Canadian Open, Osaka has not quite kicked on in 2026. While she reached the final in Bad Homburg and the quarterfinals of Wimbledon for the first time, the 29-year-old has not been able to rediscover the level that saw her win four Grand Slam titles from 2018 to 2021. Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Naomi Osaka releases statement on social media about her season In a post on Instagram , Osaka said: “Someone asked me for a season recap haha. This year has been an extreme eye-opener for me. I used to think I needed permission and approval to be myself, that I was weird for the things I wanted to express and create. “Turns out I was wrong, and the more I trusted my ideas and embraced my uniqueness, the happier and more fulfilled I became. This year is dedicated for anyone who feels a little different and is having a hard time navigating it- you’ll find yourself I promise.” Perhaps Osaka’s most impressive run in 2026 came at the Wimbledon championships, a tournament that, historically, she had struggled at. Prior to this season, Osaka had never made it past the third round of the grass court major across five appearances. But this year, Osaka made huge improvements on grass, reaching the final of the Bad Homburg Open without dropping a set. She was forced to retire during the championship match at the WTA 500 event against Karolina Muchova. Osaka’s impressive grass-court form continued into Wimbledon, where she reached the quarterfinals by beating then-world number one Aryna Sabalenka. Osaka was ultimately knocked out of the tournament by Muchova. After her run at Wimbledon, Osaka made the semifinals in Washington and the quarterfinals of the Canadian Open, but was beaten in the fourth round of the US Open by eventual champion Elena Rybakina. Osaka finished the year with an indifferent Asian swing and ended 2026 ranked 17th in the world, one spot lower than where she started the season.

item.title: A leaky AI supply chain is exposing secret user data at an alarming rate
item.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. item.title: Jonah Tong would love to join forces with ‘bulldog’ Tarik Skubal as he navigates his Mets future
item.description: David Stearns made it clear at the GM meeting this month that the Mets would acquire a starting pitcher this offseason. And at the top of that list figures to be Tarik Skubal, who met with team officials this past week as he goes after perhaps the most expensive contract for a starting pitcher in major league history. Access the Mets beat like never before Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Mike Puma about the inside buzz on the Mets. Try it free Jonah Tong, looking to secure a spot in the Mets’ rotation, doesn’t know where he’ll wind up in the team’s plans heading into 2027, but he’s well aware of what Skubal would mean to the team. “It’s the biggest talk in free agency right now and, honestly, I would love for him to come here,” Tong said. “He’s a great pitcher, obviously. Like everybody we have on our current staff, he’s just another bulldog we could have in our stable. It would be a really cool opportunity to learn from a guy as decorated as he is.” The 23-year-old Tong took part Friday in the team’s MetsGiving Turkey Giveaway at Queensborough Community College. And he knows that even without Skubal in Queens, Tong has his work cut out for himself to open the season — whenever that happens — at Citi Field. In addition to Nolan McLean, the Mets will be counting on Christian Scott and Zac Thornton, as well as Sean Manaea and Tylor Megill, who is coming back from Tommy John surgery. Mets pitcher Jonah Tong handing out turkeys at Queensborough Community College. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post Kodai Senga could also have a chance to return to the rotation . “Guys got a good glimpse of that end of the year,” Tong said of the state of the rotation. “We have a lot of really strong pieces to the foundation. I’m really excited moving forward. My job is to try to compete and contribute as much as I possibly can.” Added to the equation is the uncertainty surrounding the sport as it careens towards a lockout that is set to begin when the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches the top of the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in Los Angeles, Sunday, Aug. 16, 2026. Carlin Stiehl for CA Post Tong, who’s living with Scott this offseason in South Florida, said he’s treating this offseason as he would any other. His 2026 season ended well, when he struck out a career-high nine in his final start. Overall, though, Tong struggled and spent much of the year at Triple-A Syracuse. “It’s all lived experience,” Tong said of his season. “It was a cool way to end the year … It’s just about getting back to being myself.” Mets starting pitcher Jonah Tong throws to the Baltimore Orioles. item.title: Erie native Jon Saraceno covered Ali, Tyson and sports' biggest events
item.description: Erie native Jon Saraceno, a former USA TODAY sports columnist and prominent boxing reporter whose investigative work was nominated for a Pulitzer Prize, died Nov. 4 at Cocoa Beach, Florida, after a lengthy illness. He was 69. Shawn Sell, also a former USA TODAY journalist, confirmed her former husband’s death in an email to the Erie Times-News. More: Erie native Louis Bierbauer was Pittsburgh baseball's original Pirate Saraceno graduated from McDowell High School in 1975 and received his bachelor's degree in journalism from Penn State University in 1979. He spent the brunt of his career in that industry with Gannett Media, now USA TODAY Co. Saraceno’s sports assignments began with covering high school basketball games for The Commercial-News in Danville, Illinois. They peaked with USA TODAY assignments that included the Super Bowl, World Series, Indianapolis 500 and Olympic Games. Saraceno was also a USA TODAY sports columnist. His column, Keeping Score, was published up to three days per week. However, boxing is the sport with which Saraceno will be forever linked. Among the elites he covered and interviewed were Mike Tyson, Larry Holmes, Marvelous Marvin Hagler, Sugar Ray Leonard, Larry Holmes, Roberto Duran and Thomas Hearns. None of those encounters, though, meant more to Saraceno than forging a professional and personal relationship with his boyhood hero, Muhammad Ali. Saraceno’s sustained boxing coverage earned the Nat Fleischer Award for his excellence in boxing journalism. The award is named after the boxing historian and 1922 founder of The Ring magazine. Saraceno also received the William Randolph Hearst Investigative Reporting Award and an Associated Press Sports Editors award for his columns and investigative reporting. More: Erie boxing legend Lou Bizzarro, who fought Roberto Duran for a world title, dies at 78 Where to donate Saraceno, besides his former wife, was survived by a son, Sebastiano Saraceno, two nephews, Mark and Eric Saraceno; a niece, Julie Ritzel; two sisters-in-law, Mary Lou Noyer and her husband, Bruce, and Joyce Gunter; and a cousin, Mark Stevens. There were no calling hours or service. Burial was private. Memorial donations can be made to the Muhammad Ali Center, 144 N. 6th St., Louisville, KY 40202; Penn State University’s Bellisario College of Communications, 201 Carnegie Building, University Park, PA 16802; or Lab Rescue LRCP, P.O. Box 1814, Annandale, VA 22003. Contact Mike Copper at mcopper@timesnews.com . Follow him on X @ETNcopper. item.title: Kerby Joseph ready to roar in return to Lions: 'I'm used to being counted out'
item.description: For everyone who doubted whether he’d play football again, Kerby Joseph insists he never did. Joseph will play his first game in 406 days this Sunday, Nov. 22, when the Detroit Lions host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field. He missed the final 12 games last season with a cartilage condition in his knee and spent the first half of this season on the physically unable to perform list. Activated to the 53-man roster Wednesday, Joseph said Friday he’s ready to “crank” when he gets on the field. “I’m used to being counted out, I’m used to being doubted,” Joseph said. “It just doesn’t faze me no more. So even when it happened, I already knew I was going to be back there, even though everybody else thought I wasn’t going to be. But I already knew I was.” Joseph’s future has been a mystery since he first experienced swelling in his knee after a training camp practice last summer. He tried to play through the injury early in the season, but the Lions shut him down last October when the pain became too much to bear. He returned to practice briefly last December and said Friday the team’s decision to put him on injured reserve was the lowest point of his ordeal. “That was the first time I ever in my entire life gave up on something,” Joseph said. “Not totally gave up, but said I couldn’t go. So that was the first time ever, so I didn’t really know how to take that. But I took it with a grain of salt and then I just had a bigger chip on my shoulder ever since.” RELATED: Why Kerby Joseph still looks like a difference maker in practice Joseph bashed internet speculation his injury was career-ending – “Twitter doctors, they don’t know what I’m talking about. How you going to tell me about my body?” he said – but acknowledged Friday how meaningful it will be to play a football game again. Joseph declined to share the lengths he went to get his knee healthy this offseason, saying only, “God gave me the instruments to get back here.” “[This is] something I’ve been working hard all my life to do, and just to be back out here when the odds weren’t looking in my favor is just, man, it’s just amazing to just come out here and play with my teammates again, to play this game I love,” he said. Lions coach Dan Campbell has tried in recent weeks to temper expectations for Joseph’s return, and he did so again Friday cautioning, “there’s going to be a little rust.” “In practice there was rust when he started three weeks ago, and he’s kicked some of that off as we’ve gone here so this’ll be his first game in a minute,” Campbell said. “Don’t expect it to be perfect, but he’s a football player. And I think he’ll do some things, play within the system and be good.” Joseph said he has not experienced any knee pain since he returned to practice, and he said he expects to be the same impact player he was before his injury. “This [stuff] ain’t rusty,” he said. item.title: Tom Brady throws hat into Chelsea ownership ring with shares purchase
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Tom Brady throws hat into Chelsea ownership ring with shares purchase appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . English Premier League giants Chelsea have undergone major ownership changes behind the scenes in recent months, with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter recently selling their shares , amounting to 12.83% each, to Clearlake Capital affiliates. Now, NFL legend Tom Brady has reportedly bought minority shares in the club, according to ESPN. The seven-time Super Bowl champion had sold his 3.3% stake in Championship club Birmingham City earlier this month. Per ESPN, Defense attorney Alex Spiro is part of Brady’s ownership group and helped negotiate the deal. Brady had joined Birmingham’s ownership group as part of Knighthead Capital Management’s 2023 takeover, and also held a position on the advisory board. His departure was previously reported to be intended to help facilitate an investment into the Stamford Bridge team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brady is understood to have a strong relationship with Behdad Eghbali, co-founder and managing partner of Clearlake Capital, which now controls 86.5% of Chelsea following Boehly and Walter’s exit. The 49-year-old also holds a 5% minority stake in the NFL’s Las Vegas Raiders, alongside a minority investment in the WNBA’s Las Vegas Aces. Birmingham confirmed his departure while sitting atop the Championship table, having won League One in 2025 following relegation in 2024. Regardless, the transaction comes after Chelsea’s $3.3 billion takeover in 2022, when the consortium led by Clearlake, Boehly and Walter also committed another $2.3 billion in investment. Boehly and Walter reportedly received $1.3 billion combined for their shares in a transaction valuing the football club at approximately $6.7 billion. Chelsea currently sit fifth in the Premier League and have five wins, four losses and one draw from ten games this season thus far. The London-based club hired former player and Real Madrid manager Xabi Alonso in July 2026, and are currently sixth in the UEFA Champions League with five wins, two losses and one draw from eight games thus far. Chelsea have won a total of six First Division titles, eight FA Cups, five League Cups, and two UCL titles in their history, and are widely regarded as one of the best, and the most historic football clubs in England. item.title: Nashville SC out to complete MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield history
item.description: Nashville SC out to complete MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield history By Ben Wright NASHVILLE – In Major League Soccer's 31-year history, only eight Supporters’ Shield winners have gone on to win MLS Cup presented by Audi. Nashville SC are looking to become the ninth, starting with Sunday's Round One Best-of-3 Series opener vs. FC Cincinnati (4 pm ET | Apple TV ; FS1, FOX Deportes). The Boys in Gold made history during the regular season, setting league records for points (77), wins (23), home wins (15), goals conceded (25), and fewest losses (3). Add a Concacaf Champions Cup semifinal run in the spring, and they’ve compiled one of the best seasons in recent memory. However, Nashville know that it will all ultimately feel like a disappointment if they don’t complete an MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield double by lifting the Philip F. Anschutz Trophy on Dec. 18. "We were happy to break the record. That was the goal in the end. We achieved it, and now it's almost a new season. A new tournament starts,” club captain Hany Mukhtar said on Tuesday. “We need to be very sharp and locked in to know what is on the line, but also to know that we are the best team ever, and we should have the confidence.” ⚽🏆 ALL FOR THE CUP Every match matters. Don't miss a moment of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. Watch on Apple TV Team of destiny? It’s hard not to look at Nashville and expect them to win it all. By virtue of winning the Shield, they’ll play all but one of their Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs matches at GEODIS Park, including MLS Cup, should they reach it. They’ve been virtually automatic at their home stadium this year, going 15W-0L-2D and outscoring their opponents 48-14. They’re leaning on their experiences winning the US Open Cup in 2025 and making a run to the 2026 Concacaf Champions Cup semifinals, in which they became the first MLS team to ever win at Mexico City’s Estadio Azteca, as tangible proof that they can deliver with everything on the line. “There is a different mindset, but we have shown, last year in Open Cup and this year in the Champions League, that we are capable of knockout situations and having the pressure a little bit on,” said Mukhtar, the 2022 Landon Donovan MLS MVP. “At the end of the day, there's nothing to fear. We have beaten all of them. We just need to do what we do best.” At the same time, Nashville know they have a target on their backs and history against them. While Shield winners rarely lift MLS Cup, there's some modern-day MLS precedent after LAFC completed the double in 2022. “We look at this as an extension of the regular season; we want to continue to do the same preparation, the same process of how we're gonna prepare for an opponent,” said head coach B.J. Callaghan. “I think this team is a team that maybe history hasn't had to always define it. Our guys are focused on understanding that the guarantee that we have is a three-game series. The whole regular season has earned ourselves just a three-game series.” Elite defense Nashvill

item.title: Waste crisis: Acting LAWMA MD resumes, reads riot act to staff
item.description: .unveils 60-day action plan ​By Olasunkanmi Akoni Amid mounting concerns over waste management across the metropolis, the newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has assumed office with a stern warning to the workforce, reading the riot act against laxity. Akinyemi, also unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to clear backlogs and restore the agency’s past glory. ​Addressing management and staff at a tense workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s Ijora-Olopa headquarters on Friday, he made it clear that business as usual was over. Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi, the new helmsman demanded total commitment, positive work ethics, and renewed dedication to duty from every personnel, warning that repositioning the agency requires uncompromising discipline and active participation from all ranks. ​”We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. “We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi declared, signaling zero tolerance for operational inefficiencies. ​To back up his charge, Akinyemi rolled out a 60-day blueprint aimed at rapid waste evacuation, stricter regulatory enforcement, and aggressive field monitoring across Lagos State. While giving key highlights of the emergency plan, the MD boss said personnel will be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with local terrains to sharpen field monitoring and speed up response times. Hinting on decentralised operational hubs, Akinyemi added that the hubs will be established to decentralise waste management, tighten supervision, and bring rapid intervention closer to blackspots requiring urgent attention. On ​indiscriminate dumping, he avowed the agency’s determination to intensify community sensitization on waste sorting at source, mobilizing traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations, and artisans to enforce responsible disposal habits. Akinyemi, therefore, called for closer synergy with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and demanded stricter public compliance with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain operations. ​While reading the riot act on performance, the Acting MD also moved to boost morale, assuring workers that their welfare remains a top priority. item.title: Dave Portnoy Threatens to Sue the NY Times For Quoting Him
item.description: Screenshot via Barstool Sports Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy threatened legal action against The New York Times on Friday after the newspaper quoted his own public remarks in a story about the disastrous first season of Michigan football coach Kyle Whittingham . Portnoy, a University of Michigan alumnus and die-hard Wolverines fan, took issue with a Friday report by The Athletic , the Times -owned sports outlet, examining how Whittingham’s once-celebrated hiring has turned into a nightmare for the program. “I did not give the @nytimes permission to use an old quote of mine. Please delete or you’ll be hearing from my lawyers,” Portnoy wrote on X. I did not give the @nytimes permission to use an old quote of mine. Please delete or you’ll be hearing from my lawyers pic.twitter.com/VlJQixbVtg — Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) November 20, 2026 The offending quote? Three words Portnoy enthusiastically exclaimed in a video he posted publicly in December 2025, shortly after Michigan hired Whittingham. “Kyle Whittingham! Yes!” Michigan hires Kyle Whittingham and just like that the kings of college football are back on top! What a spectacular hire! I can’t wait to get my hands on some big nasty Samoans! #GoBlue pic.twitter.com/iXX8ZH000k — Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) December 26, 2025 The Athletic’s Austin Meek and Bruce Feldman included the remark near the beginning of their lengthy examination of Michigan’s struggles, highlighting how the hiring initially drew widespread praise from prominent voices in college football. But Michigan has stumbled to a 5-5 record through Whittingham’s first 10 games, with an offense so ineffective that the school fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck after just nine games. The report detailed growing discontent among players, parents and former staffers, including concerns that Whittingham’s efforts to import his Utah coaching philosophy have clashed with Michigan’s established traditions. Portnoy’s legal threat, meanwhile, quickly drew a public fact-check. An X Community Note attached to his post pointed out that the disputed quote came directly from his own publicly available video, which was captioned, “Michigan hires Kyle Whittingham and just like that the kings of college football are back on top! What a spectacular hire!”. “Portnoy’s ‘Kyle Whittingham! Yes!’ quote is from his own public Dec. 2025 X post/video celebrating the hire. News outlets do not require permission to quote public statements by public figures,” the note read. The post Dave Portnoy Threatens to Sue the NY Times For Quoting Him first appeared on Mediaite .

item.title: New NASA Seed Funding Primes Small Businesses for Innovation
item.description: Illustration of a future lunar vehicle that could potentially be powered by NASA-funded research, now under way, to develop an ultra-cold-tolerant battery module. Elementium Materials Inc. Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. This early-stage research and development work will tackle an array of topics, including those related to Artemis and the establishment of a U.S. Moon Base . Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies. Following are a few examples of research supported through these recent awards: Bringing Power to Moon and Mars An SBIR Phase II award for Opterus Research and Development Inc. supports a project focused on bringing power to the surface of the Moon and Mars by developing a modular system of rollable solar arrays. The arrays can be handled robotically, are compatible with various support structures, and work even in dusty surface conditions. The technology could be scaled up to 50 kilowatts, and it could provide a reliable power source to help both NASA and commercial space companies develop infrastructure on the Moon . Rovers With Reach: Vision and Tactile Sensing in Robotic Arm This SBIR Phase I award, led by Intelligent Fiber Optic Systems Corporation, aims to help lunar rovers perform complex tasks independently on the Moon. The firm’s 10-foot, extendable robotic arm can both “see” and has a sense of touch, combining a camera with sensors to detect and measure surface textures, contact forces, and temperature. The technology could help automate many lunar surface tasks, such as cleaning solar panels, positioning habitat structures, and collecting scientific samples from hard-to-reach locations. item.title: Mildly interesting players are being non-tendered
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - SEPTEMBER 07: Nolan Gorman #16 of the St. Louis Cardinals looks on prior to the game between the St. Louis Cardinals and the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on Monday, September 7, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Kavin Mistry/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The deadline for MLB teams to tender contracts to players who are on the 40 man roster but not currently under contract is 4 p.m. Central today. Players who are not tendered a contract by that time will become free agents. This provides one of the nerdy kind of exciting times in the offseason — a meatier, more substantive version of the Rule 5 Draft. We get to speculate as to what arb-eligible players may be cut loose by teams that do not want to risk the player getting a salary in arbitration in excess of what the team thinks the player is worth. We get to see what contracts are announced today, thus learning which players were in danger of being non-tendered if they didn’t agree to a contract before the deadline. And there will be a spate of players who will hit the free agent market and make us say, oh, hey, he’s a free agent, My Favorite Team should try to sign him. Usually that desire for Your Favorite Team to sign said player is dampened once you take a look at his recent performance level and/or injury history, but still, that bit of frisson when you see a name that once was associated with something of value being out there and available is something we can all enjoy in these noisome November nights. Take, for instance, Nolan Gorman. He was the Cardinals’ first round pick in 2018, taken four picks after the Rangers selected Cole Winn. Keith Law actually mocked Gorman to the Rangers in one of his mock drafts that year.* He was a consensus top-100 prospect from 2019-22, and was a consensus top-35 prospect in 2022. In 2023 he put up an 805 OPS with 27 home runs. And he’s reportedly being non-tendered. The Rangers should jump all over him! * In searching to see if I had done a draft preview of Gorman that year, I found this write-up I did in 2019 of someone named Jimmy Lewis. For the life of me, I have no memory of doing this write-up, or of this Jimmy Lewis guy ever existing. Alas, he’s kind of been bad since then. He’s played second base and third base, neither of them well, and after slashing .204/.284/.385 in the 2024-25 seasons, Gorman ended up splitting 2026 between the majors and AAA, slashing .184/.272/.308 in the former and .182/.328/.430 in the latter. So yeah, you can see how he’s ended up in the late-November second wave of free agents. Along those same lines, the Twins are reportedly non-tendering Bailey Ober and Trevor Larnach, each of whom were entering their final season of arbitration eligibility, and each of whom would seem to be in line for high-seven-figure 2027 salaries via the arbitration process. item.title: Chris Russo fears entire 2027 MLB season is ‘in jeopardy’
item.description: Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Less than three months after saying he’s confident there will be a 2027 Major League Baseball season, Christopher “Mad Dog” Russo is worried. We’ve known baseball was heading toward a lockout for about as long as we’ve known the current collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the MLB players was set to expire after the 2026 season. Even while knowing a lengthy lockout was looming, Russo confidently predicted there will be a 2027 MLB season this past September. But we haven’t even made it to the lockout yet, and Russo is already changing his tune. In recent weeks, commissioner Rob Manfred has maintained the owners will not compromise on their desire to institute a salary cap. The players, meanwhile, have refused to even entertain a CBA proposal from the owners that includes a salary cap. And with no room for negotiation on the horizon, Russo expressed doubt about baseball being played in 2027 during an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show on Friday morning. ﻿ “The players are not going to engage in these last proposals,” Russo told Patrick. “Because if they do that, then they’re basically telling you that we’ll deal with the salary cap.” Russo noted this is likely heading to court, with the players possibly seeking to file a disclaimer of interest to dissolve the union, allowing them to pursue antitrust lawsuits against the league. “If they win, there’s going to be an appeal. If they lose their appeal, this could take forever,” Russo continued. “I don’t talk to the owners, but I do believe they’re very committed to getting this done.” There is some precedent for PA’s filing a disclaimer of interest. The NBPA did it during the 2011 NBA lockout, dissolving the union on Nov. 14 before quickly reaching a tentative CBA agreement on Nov. 26. But MLB owners and players seem further apart on an agreement with a salary cap on the line. And Russo insists MLB is in a better position to institute a salary cap now than they were during the strike shortened season in 1994, because currently, they’re a league ran by lawyers. “Unlike ’94 with [Bud] Selig, who wasn’t a lawyer, they got good lawyers. Manfred’s a lawyer. He want to Harvard Law School. Dan Halem, his right hand-hand man went to Cornell… they got that buttoned-up. And I think they feel the union can’t win in court, so as a result of that, the union’s going to have to fight that in court, and so, this is going to take forever. But I do believe, the owners are very, very committed to getting this fixed once and for all.” “I believe it needs to be fixed. That’s my opinion. Some people would disagree, but I think this is going to be a very long, drawn out process,” Russo added. “It’s a long way to go. It’s Nov. 20. I think the ’27 season is in jeopardy. I really do. The whole season.” MLB owners are more united than ever

item.title: I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2. item.title: Kalen DeBoer Makes Bold Declaration About His Alabama Football Team
item.description: STARKVILLE, MISSISSIPPI - OCTOBER 03: Head coach Kalen DeBoer of the Alabama Crimson Tide looks on before the game against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Starkville, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) Getty Alabama football head coach Kalen DeBoer isn’t backing down from expectations surrounding the Crimson Tide. In fact, as his third season in Tuscaloosa progresses, DeBoer believes he’s finally assembled the most complete team of his tenure. Speaking with ESPN’s Alex Scarborough, DeBoer explained why this year’s Alabama team is different from the previous two and why he believes the Crimson Tide are equipped to compete with anyone in college football. “I feel like we’re more complete as a football team and able to play anybody, anytime, anywhere,” DeBoer told ESPN. “But you got to go do it.” It’s a confident statement from a head coach who understands better than most that expectations at Alabama don’t come with much room for error. But there’s also an important distinction in DeBoer’s comments. He’s not simply suggesting Alabama has more talent. He’s pointing to something that has taken three seasons to develop. Kalen DeBoer Explains Why This Alabama Team Is Different When DeBoer arrived in Tuscaloosa in January 2024, he inherited one of the most unusual situations in college football. He wasn’t replacing a coach who had been fired after an unsuccessful tenure. He was replacing Nick Saban, who had delivered six national championships to Alabama before retiring following the 2023 season. The transition brought significant roster movement, a new coaching staff and an entirely different offensive and defensive philosophy. DeBoer’s first Alabama team had plenty of experience and talent, but those players were learning an entirely new system. The second season presented almost the opposite challenge. While the Crimson Tide had developed a stronger understanding of DeBoer’s expectations, schemes and overall approach, the roster lacked some of the experience that had been present during his first year. Now, in Year 3, DeBoer believes those two critical elements have finally come together. Alabama has a roster that combines experience with familiarity in the system, giving the Crimson Tide a level of continuity that simply wasn’t available during the first two seasons. That combination could be the most significant development of DeBoer’s tenure. Alabama’s Growth Goes Beyond Talent and Experience Perhaps the most interesting takeaway from DeBoer’s conversation with ESPN wasn’t necessarily his confidence in the roster. It was his emphasis on the team’s resilience. According to Scarborough, DeBoer has noticed the development of a deeper roster and a more resilient mindset among his players. That’s an important distinction for an Alabama program that has experienced its share of adversity during the transition from Saban to DeBoer. item.title: 'They are frightened of winning' - Antonio Conte hits back after missing out on Man Utd job to Mauricio Pochettino ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: SSC Napoli v Udinese Calcio - Serie A - Getty Images Sport Antonio Conte has launched a stinging critique of Manchester United following the club's decision to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their new permanent manager. The Italian tactician, who was heavily linked with the vacancy at Old Trafford, suggested that the hierarchy's hesitation to hire him reflects a deeper issue within the club. Conte questions United's ambition Conte has hit out at clubs that decide against hiring him , suggesting they are 'frightened of winning' due to his notoriously demanding and intense coaching style. The 57-year-old was widely considered a frontrunner for the Manchester United job following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, but the Premier League giants ultimately chose to appoint former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino instead. Known for his uncompromising approach and high-intensity tactical drills, Conte has a proven track record of success, having secured five Serie A titles alongside a Premier League trophy during his tenure at Chelsea. However, it appears his reputation for being a volatile and difficult figure to manage may have played a role in United's decision to look elsewhere for their long-term project. Respect for the Ferguson legacy Despite his frustrations with the recent hiring process - which saw United turn to Pochettino amid a slump in form that leaves them 18th in the Premier League table with eight points and just one win from their opening 10 matches - Conte was quick to express his profound admiration for Sir Alex Ferguson. 'Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature. They last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson. I've read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football,' Conte told Cronache di spogliatoio. A methodology built for victory Addressing the critics who claim his personality and training requirements are too taxing for modern squads - coming after his last role coaching Napoli, whom he guided to second place in Serie A behind Inter last season before leaving the club by mutual consent at the conclusion of the campaign - Conte remained defiant. 'If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer. That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it's as if someone were placing a veto on the club's return to its own history. A method is what's needed to achieve major results. And if you're suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players,' he added. item.title: Chivas' five aims for the end of the Apertura 2026
item.description: Chivas' five aims for the end of the Apertura 2026 Guadalajara will face Cruz Azul on Matchday 17 of the Apertura 2026 with a chance to cap off an impressive regular season. Along with seeking an important win in front of their home fans, the Sacred Flock have five key objectives heading into their final match of the tournament. 1. Chasing the top spot Chivas have a chance to finish at the top of the standings. To do so, they need to beat Cruz Azul and hope América lose or draw their match. 2. Finishing with the best home record in the Apertura 2026 Estadio AKRON has been an important venue for Guadalajara, who will look to finish with the most points at home. So far, they have collected 16 of a possible 24 points, with five wins, one draw and two losses, earning 66.7% of the available points and scoring 15 goals. 3. Securing the best defensive record With just 15 goals conceded, the Sacred Flock have all but secured the best defensive record in the league. Their closest challengers have conceded 20 goals, giving Guadalajara a five-goal advantage in this category. 4. Staying unbeaten away from home Guadalajara will also finish the Apertura 2026 as the only team unbeaten away from home. They recorded three wins and five draws in their eight away matches, a record that reflects their consistency throughout the regular season. 5. item.title: McInnes To Make Changes? | Predicted 4-4-2 Rangers Lineup To Face Motherwell
item.description: McInnes To Make Changes? | Predicted 4-4-2 Rangers Lineup To Face Motherwell Despite their comprehensive win over St Mirren in Paisley, Rangers have dropped points in their recent outings away from home. Another tricky test on the road awaits Derek McInnes’ men, with the Light Blues set for a trip to North Lanarkshire to lock horns with Motherwell on Saturday night. The Well dominated this fixture last season, claiming one win and two draws in four Premiership encounters. However, they lost at Ibrox in September’s reverse tie, and with just one victory in their last nine games, young Swedish boss Alfred Johansson has found his side battling for survival at the wrong end of the league standings. Nevertheless, the Steelmen enjoyed a three-game unbeaten streak before the international break, and it remains to be seen whether the momentum is maintained this weekend. Ivor Pandur has been a shining light between the sticks, as the Croatian custodian made some stellar saves while clinching back-to-back clean sheets against Aberdeen and St Mirren. He must show his supremacy in goal and help his side snatch all three points to keep pace with Old Firm rivals Celtic. GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – DECEMBER 27: Youssef Chermiti of Rangers attempts a shot at goal during the Premier League match between Rangers and Motherwell at Ibrox Stadium on December 27, 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Rangers have a stable backline, with Dujon Sterling likely to retain the right-back spot ahead of Kosta Nedeljkovic. Centre-half Ben Godfrey and left-back Tuur Rommens started the campaign as the preferred options, but have lost their place following Olwethu Makhanya and James Penrice’s emergence during Godfrey and Rommens’ brief injury layoffs. They must feature again in their respective roles, and so should Emmanuel Fernandez, who has been a revelation in deep defence since his low-key arrival last year from Peterborough United. Midfield McInnes has found stability in the middle of the park, with Nicolas Raskin and Dan Neil offering the right balance and technicality. Their defensive contribution, box-to-box runs, and link-up play would frustrate the home side in their efforts to dominate the midfield battle. Cammy Devlin and Ross McCrorie remain sidelined, but they have Vanja Dragojevic and Tochi Chukwuani, who could feature from the bench at some point in the second half. Badredine Bouanani has made a positive impact since his late transfer from VfB Stuttgart on a season-long loan. The Algerian should operate from the right, allowing versatile Min-Su Kim to occupy the left midfield role over Findlay Curtis and Djeidi Gassama. Ryan Naderi and Kevin Kelsy have stepped in as the centre-forward pairing amid injuries to Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti. Bojan Miovski would continue as the understudy to the first-team duo, as he has found his minutes limited high up the pitch.

item.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
item.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain
item.description: SpaceX's successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA's path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-important, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year. For SpaceX's purposes, Saturday's mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX's deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon. Early next year, SpaceX plans to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX's existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. item.title: Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO
item.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday. The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday. The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said that the incident was not a system collapse. It said that the disturbance resulted from the tripping of some transmission line, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”NISO wishes to clarify that the grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse. “It resulted from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”At 12:34 p.m., the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex. ”Subsequently, at 12:50 p.m, the Ihovbor–Oshogbo transmission line tripped alongside the Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in load losses in some parts of the country,” it said. The system operator said that prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilize the grid and restore affected transmission lines. It said that all the affected lines had since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49 p.m. on Friday. It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations, and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid. ”The public is advised to rely on official communications from NISO for accurate information on developments within the national electricity grid,” it said. (NAN) The post Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Afenifere demands prosecution of sponsors of campaign violence
item.description: …Raises alarm over rising attacks ahead of 2027 elections By Adeola Badru The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has raised the alarm over increasing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling for the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators and their sponsors. The organisation warned that the growing incidents of thuggery, intimidation and inflammatory political rhetoric posed a serious threat to the country’s democratic process. Afenifere, in a statement issued on Friday by its National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, called on political parties, candidates, their sponsors and supporters to end violence and ensure that campaigns were conducted in accordance with the Constitution and the Electoral Act. Ajayi expressed concern over reported attacks on political figures, campaign convoys and supporters in different parts of the country, warning that the growing atmosphere of hostility could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and endanger lives. Among the incidents cited was the reported attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu on Friday, November 13, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Central Mosque, Abuja. According to the organisation, assailants threw stones and other dangerous objects at the departing presidential convoy, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives. Afenifere also condemned the attack on supporters of the Accord Party governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, around the Molete area of Ibadan, which reportedly resulted in the death of a 40-year-old supporter, Azeez Tajudeen. It described the incident as particularly disturbing, saying the destruction of vehicles and loss of life highlighted the consequences of allowing political differences to degenerate into violence. The organisation further listed the reported attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State; the reported assault on the convoy of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Calabar, Cross River State; and disruptions of political gatherings, particularly those of the APC and ADC in Sokoto, Kebbi and Lagos states. It said the incidents reflected a disturbing pattern requiring urgent intervention by political leaders and security agencies. Ajayi also recalled the warning by former President Goodluck Jonathan at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Peace Conference in Abuja, where he cautioned political leaders against running their parties like rival cult groups. Jonathan had warned against recruiting and exploiting young Nigerians for political violence, saying such practices could plunge the country into avoidable crises. Similarly, Senate President Godswill Akpabio had cautioned youths against allowing themselves to be used for political violence, warning that perpetrators could face serious criminal charges, including treasonable felony. item.title: Obi woos Onitsha voters, promises jobs, better services
item.description: …Says Nigeria needs energetic president By Vincent Ujumadu The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday drew a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall meeting in the commercial city. Obi began his visit with a stop at his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he told students that the institution had produced three state governors and could soon produce Nigeria’s president. The three former governors he identified were Peter Odili of Rivers State, Obi himself and Willie Obiano, who succeeded him as governor of Anambra State. Addressing the students, Obi promised to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in the 2027 general elections. His campaign train subsequently moved through Oguta Road, Upper Iweka, Head Bridge, Uga Road and Modebe Avenue before arriving at All Saints Cathedral, venue of the town hall meeting. Among those who accompanied him during the roadshow were Aisha Yesufu and other members of his campaign team. Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign music, while several traders reportedly closed their shops to attend the town hall meeting. Addressing supporters at the gathering, Obi said he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, had formed a team committed to uniting the country, tackling insecurity and corruption, and ensuring that public resources were used for the benefit of Nigerians. “Kwankwaso and I have formed a team that will unite and secure Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, fight corruption and use public money for public good. “I assure Nigerians that from day one, they will be feeling the good impact of their country. You will know that a new team is in charge,” he said. He promised to move Nigeria from a consumption-driven economy to one centred on production, create employment opportunities and invest in critical sectors. “We cannot continue with the present situation where our children don’t have jobs because that is not the way a country should be,” he said. On healthcare, Obi advocated a system where Nigerians could access functional medical facilities without having to depend on religious institutions for treatment. He pledged to establish functional primary healthcare centres in every ward and said his proposed administration would build 10,000 healthcare centres across the country. He also promised that his administration would commence the construction of 40,000 classroom blocks from its first day in office, alongside increased investment in education and healthcare. On electricity, the former Anambra governor expressed concern over Nigeria’s power generation capacity, which he put at about 5,000 megawatts. item.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
item.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns

item.title: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons. Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing : The pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts. CTIA said the pilot test shows "that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications." item.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
item.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. On data protection, Oyedele called on financial institutions to strengthen safeguards around customers’ personal and financial information to protect them against fraud and other abuses. item.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
item.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." item.title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
item.description: …Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said. item.title: ‘I won’t disappoint you in my second term’ – Adeleke assures Osun people
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration. A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying. Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy. According to him, the Osun election that re-elected Governor Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it. “That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people,” he submitted on behalf of the Chief Imam of Osogboland, Sheikh Musa Animasahun. The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Hon. Teslim Igbalaye; Osun Central Accord Senatorial candidate, Hon. Ganiyu Olaoluwa; members of the state executive council; special advisers; and top government functionaries.
